yucky adjective and interjection

also yuck, icky, gross, eww, ugh, phew (bad smell), pooh, what a stink

classical

Lucr. 1.936: absinthia taetra
Caes. BC 3.49 (Lewis & Short)

taeter, taetra, taetrum

adjective · Declension on Wiktionary

nasty, foul (to taste, smell or sight)

Lucretius’s word for the bitter wormwood that doctors give children.

Other words

  • foedus, foeda, foedum — foul, disgusting, ugly

    adjective · also used · classical · Plin. NH 29.61: cīmicēs foedissimum animal (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

  • pūtidus, pūtida, pūtidum — rotten, stinking

    adjective · also used · classical · Cic. Pis. 19: carō (Lewis & Short); Plaut. Bacch. 4.7.23: fungus (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

    Of food gone off.

  • 1fu: vowel length unsettled, left unmarked. Lewis & Short marks neither fu nor fue, only the variant fūfae that it cites from Charisius; the two places in Plautus were not scanned for this entry.

    Fu!1 (Fue!) — ugh! (disgust)

    interjection · also used · classical · Plaut. Most. 1.1.37 (Lewis & Short); Plaut. Ps. 5.2.5 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 359 · Wiktionary

    (vōx cōmica: Plaut.)

    Lewis & Short: “denoting aversion, foh! fie!”. In the Mostellaria, at a slave who reeks of garlic.

  • Apage! — take it away! (refusing something)

    interjection · also used · classical · Plaut. Am. 2.1.32: apage tē ā mē (Lewis & Short); Ter. Eun. 4.6.18: apage sīs (Lewis & Short) · Wiktionary

    (vōx cōmica: Plaut., Ter.; apud Cicerōnem numquam)

Examples

  • sed vel utī puerīs absinthia taetra medentēs cum dare cōnantur, prius ōrās pōcula circum contingunt mellis dulcī flāvōque liquōre

    but as doctors, when they try to give children nasty wormwood, first coat the rims of the cups with the sweet golden liquid of honeyLucr. 1.936–938

  • Fī! Quidnam est iste fētor?

    Phew! What’s that stench?Traupman 359

See also bitter, taste, hate, bah!.
